title: Labour market: supply factors and immobility

stages.name: Labour market: supply factors and immobility
stages.title: Labour market: supply factors and immobility
stages.sub: Explain why the supply of labour to a job or area can be limited, and why workers cannot always move to where jobs are.

steps.q: A country has a rise in working-age migrants arriving and settling. What happens to the number of people available to work?

steps.q: Electricians must complete years of training before they can legally practise. Does this training requirement make it easy or hard for new people to start working as electricians?
steps.right: It makes it harder to start
steps.wrong: It makes no difference either way
steps.hint: Think about someone with no training trying to become an electrician tomorrow.

steps.q: On top of the training requirement, a union now refuses to let new electricians join easily. What happens to the number of people able to supply their labour as electricians?
steps.right: It stays lower than it otherwise would be
steps.wrong: It rises to match demand for electricians
steps.hint: Qualifications already restrict entry. Does an extra restriction on joining make entry easier or harder?

steps.q: Benefits are cut and income tax is lowered for low earners. Would more or fewer people be willing to take a job now?
steps.right: More people would be willing to work
steps.wrong: The same number would be willing to work
steps.hint: Think about how much better off someone is now from working versus not working.

steps.q: A factory worker in Newcastle is offered a job in London, but rents there are far higher and their family lives near Newcastle. Can they easily take the job?
steps.right: No, moving is difficult for them
steps.wrong: Yes, they can move without any problem
steps.hint: Think about what is stopping them physically relocating, even though they want the job.

steps.q: A coal miner loses their job when the mine closes. They have no training in other fields and struggle to get interviews in new industries. Can they simply switch into a different occupation straight away?
steps.right: No, their skills do not transfer to other jobs
steps.wrong: Yes, they can switch occupation easily
steps.hint: Think about whether their existing skills are useful in a different type of job.

steps.q: Both workers want a job but cannot get to it or into it, one blocked by distance and cost, the other by mismatched skills. What do these two problems both show about labour?
steps.right: Labour cannot move freely to where it is needed
steps.wrong: Labour always moves freely to where it is needed
